subject: Conversational session resets — interim status & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex@scribehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T14:05:00Z
Subject: Interrupted streaming — multiple session resets during long conversations

Hi Naomi,

We started seeing intermittent session resets in production around 13:50 UTC that cause our users' long-running conversational sessions to drop mid-stream. The client sees repeated 'session_reset' messages and then the stream terminates; when the client reconnects it receives a fresh conversation id and the KV cache is empty. This is impacting a small subset of high-throughput customers (primarily our note-taking flow).

Attached is a short server-side dump (session_dump_1130.log) and a sequence of client-side events. Key observations:
- Reset frequency: ~1-3 resets per 10k sessions in us-east-1 between 13:50–14:10 UTC
- Symptoms: websocket disconnect followed by an immediate new websocket with new session id; older session's KV cache missing on reconnect
- Impact: partial transcript loss for end-users; retries lead to duplicate tokens billed

Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side, and if there's an ETA for mitigation? We have an executive check-in at 16:00 UTC and need to tell them the plan.

Thanks,
Alex Monroe
Head of Integrations
ScribeHealth

Attachment: session_dump_1130.log (text, 48KB)

Ben, Rishi — forwarding ScribeHealth's report. They see session resets + KV cache loss on reconnect in us-east-1. Ticket opened on internal side: INC-6128.

Initial triage notes:
- Preliminary logs show session-manager process restarting on a subset of hosts in the us-east-1 serving pool at ~13:49–13:55 UTC.
- Restart correlates with a cache-compaction cycle that kicks in when prefix-cache memory crosses threshold after a burst of long-conversation requests. We need to confirm whether the restart is a hard process exit (OOM) or a voluntary restart due to assert in session housekeeping.

Immediate asks:
1) Ben — can you grab the session-manager logs for host group east-api-22 and check for oom-kill / segfault / assert lines?
2) Rishi — can you evaluate whether we can route ScribeHealth's traffic to a warm dedicated pool as a mitigation (low-friction) and whether that will preserve KV cache on reconnects?
3) I'll provide a short customer-facing status update once we have confirmation.

Naomi

Subject: Re: Interrupted streaming — interim mitigation in place

Alex — quick update from our side. Thank you for the logs; they were very helpful.

What we know (interim):
- Root symptom: session-manager on a small subset of us-east-1 hosts is restarting during a cache-compaction window. The restart clears in-memory KV caches for active sessions and manifests as a session reset on the client.
- Mitigation deployed (15:05 UTC): we routed ScribeHealth traffic to a dedicated warm pool that isolates long-running conversational sessions and preserves in-memory KV on reconnects. This should stop the immediate user-facing resets.
- Short-term recommendation for your client: enable client retry with idempotency tokens and increase websocket reconnect backoff to 500–1500ms to avoid duplicate token billing in the interim.

We are continuing to investigate whether the restart is due to memory pressure or a race during compaction. Ben is pulling full process traces; Rishi's team is validating the dedicated-pool route and will monitor p99 reconnects.

We have also published a brief mitigation playbook weve attached (mitigation_playbook.md) for your engineering team to tune their client-side retry behavior.

I'll follow up with a consolidated timeline and a link to the incident page once we have a confirmed root cause and remediation plan. Next update planned by 16:30 UTC or sooner if we escalate.

Apologies for the disruption and thank you for flagging this quickly.

Best,
Naomi
Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident wrap & postmortem link — session-manager restart during cache compaction

Alex — final update and link to the postmortem doc. Thanks again for your patience.

Timeline (summary):
- 13:49 UTC — first observed client disconnects for long-running sessions in us-east-1
- 13:50–14:00 UTC — session-manager restarts observed on 3 hosts in east-api-22 during scheduled cache-compaction window
- 15:05 UTC — traffic for ScribeHealth routed to dedicated warm pool (mitigation)
- 17:20 UTC — fix merged to main that prevents the compaction race that caused the restart; validated in canary; full rollout planned 11/30 02:00 UTC

Root cause: a race condition in session-manager's compaction routine where an in-progress prefix-cache swap could trigger a double-free path under bursty long-session workloads, leading to process termination and in-memory KV eviction.

Impact: intermittent session resets and KV cache loss for a small fraction of long-running conversational sessions in us-east-1. We estimate customer-facing impact for ScribeHealth at ~0.8% of sessions during the 20-minute window.

Remediation & next steps:
- Code fix merged to block the compaction double-free and to add an assert-suppression path for safe compaction (rollout 11/30 02:00 UTC).
- Increased observability: additional metrics around compaction duration and in-progress swap counts; alerting thresholds added.
- Operational: auto-evacuate hosts before compaction when KV working set exceeds threshold; improve canary gating for compaction changes.
- Customer support: we will issue a small credit for token duplication caused by retries. Naomi will follow up with billing.

Postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood.example/postmortems/session-reset-20261129 (attached: postmortem-draft.pdf)
Status page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2026-11-29-session-reset

If you'd like a short run-through of the postmortem, happy to jump on a call — otherwise we'll send a final postmortem when the doc is validated by engineering and QA.

Thanks,
